parts.answer: The y-gain sets the voltage represented by each vertical division.
accepted_alternatives: It converts vertical divisions into voltage.

marking_points.text: States that y-gain gives voltage per vertical division or converts vertical divisions to voltage.

parts.answer: The time-base sets the time represented by each horizontal division.
accepted_alternatives: It converts horizontal divisions into time.

marking_points.text: States that time-base gives time per horizontal division or converts horizontal divisions to time.

option_feedback.A: Amplitude is a positive maximum size, not the negative extreme displacement.
option_feedback.B: Zero is the equilibrium displacement, not the amplitude.
option_feedback.C: Correct. The maximum displacement from equilibrium is 6.0 mm.

marking_points.text: Selects C, giving the amplitude as 6.0 mm.

option_feedback.A: This divides the scale by the division count instead of multiplying.
option_feedback.C: This doubles the correct amplitude, as if using peak-to-peak height.
option_feedback.D: This treats divisions per volt as volts per division.

marking_points.text: Selects B, using 3.5 × 0.20 V div⁻¹ = 0.70 V.

option_feedback.A: 2.0 ms is the period value before conversion and reciprocal, not a frequency.
option_feedback.B: This multiplies the division count by a value interpreted incorrectly as hertz.
option_feedback.C: Correct. T = 2.0 ms = 2.0 × 10⁻³ s and f = 500 Hz.
option_feedback.D: This takes the reciprocal of 0.50 ms rather than the full-cycle time.

marking_points.text: Selects C, obtaining 500 Hz from a period of 2.0 ms.
Multiplies 2.8 vertical divisions by 50 mV div⁻¹.
Obtains 0.140 V with a valid voltage unit.

parts.answer: Two cycles take 7.5 × 0.80 ms = 6.0 ms, so T = 6.0 ms / 2 = 3.0 ms = 3.0 × 10⁻³ s.

marking_points.text: Uses 7.5 × 0.80 ms for two cycles and divides by two.
Obtains 3.0 × 10⁻³ s with a valid time unit.
Uses the three-division centre-to-crest height and y-gain to obtain 0.75 V.
Multiplies the four-division cycle width by 0.50 ms div⁻¹.
Obtains 2.0 × 10⁻³ s with a valid time unit.
Uses f = 1/T with the period in seconds.
Obtains 500 Hz with a valid frequency unit.

parts.answer: Amplitude is half the peak-to-peak height: (5.6/2) × 0.15 = 0.42 V.

marking_points.text: Halves the 5.6-division peak-to-peak height to obtain a 2.8-division amplitude.
Uses y-gain to obtain 0.42 V with a valid voltage unit.

parts.answer: Four cycles take 14.4 × 20 μs = 288 μs. T = 288 μs / 4 = 72 μs = 7.2 × 10⁻⁵ s. f = 1/T = 1.39 × 10⁴ Hz.

marking_points.text: Uses 14.4 × 20 μs for four cycles and divides by four to obtain T = 72 μs.
Converts the period to 7.2 × 10⁻⁵ s and uses f = 1/T.
Obtains 1.39 × 10⁴ Hz or 13.9 kHz with a valid frequency unit.
States that the progressive sound wave transfers energy from source to microphone.
